C001.reason: Field renamed from SpeedMps to SpeedKph; must scale request.Speed (m/s) by 3.6 before assigning to SpeedKph field.

C002.reason: Output key renamed from speed_mps to speed_kph; value must be entity.SpeedKph from parsed entity.

C003.reason: Speeding threshold changes from >30.0 to >108.0 (after unit conversion); must use entity.SpeedKph for comparison.

edits.before: var sample = new Simulation.Telemetry.VehicleTelemetry { VehicleId = request.VehicleId, SpeedMps = (float)request.Speed };
edits.after: var sample = new Simulation.Telemetry.VehicleTelemetry { VehicleId = request.VehicleId, SpeedKph = (float)(request.Speed * 3.6) };

edits.before: var fields = new Dictionary<string, object> { ["vehicle_id"] = entity.VehicleId, ["speed_mps"] = entity.SpeedMps };
edits.after: var fields = new Dictionary<string, object> { ["vehicle_id"] = entity.VehicleId, ["speed_kph"] = entity.SpeedKph };

edits.before: return new { fields, speeding = entity.SpeedMps > 30.0, constructed_payload = Convert.ToBase64String(sample.ToByteArray()) };
edits.after: return new { fields, speeding = entity.SpeedKph > 108.0, constructed_payload = Convert.ToBase64String(sample.ToByteArray()) };

rationale: The schema change renames speed_mps to speed_kph with unit change from m/s to km/h. Producer must scale input by 3.6 before serialization. Consumer observes speed_kph in output JSON. Speeding threshold updates from 30 m/s (108 km/h) to 108 km/h directly using the converted value. All three candidates require modifications to align with the new field name, unit, and threshold.
assumptions: The regenerated protobuf bindings expose SpeedKph property for field 2
Entity.SpeedKph is populated correctly when parsing base64 payload
JSON output uses double-precision JSON numbers for float32 values
No mixed version/unit scenarios to handle
